evidence_chain: [Fact] TSMC official Q1 2026 quarterly results page reports Q1 2026 revenue of US$35.90B. Source: https://investor.tsmc.com/english/quarterly-results/2026/q1

[Fact] TSMC Q1 2026 management report states that 7nm-and-below technologies accounted for 74% of wafer revenue and HPC represented 61% of revenue. Source: https://investor.tsmc.com/english/encrypt/files/encrypt_file/reports/2026-04/5508a9df8981f587c73dbfaf9f577f142e22bbb1/1Q26ManagementReport.pdf

[Fact] TSMC Q1 2026 earnings release reports consolidated Q1 revenue of NT$1,134.10B, net income of NT$572.48B and EPS of NT$22.08; it also states advanced technologies accounted for 74% of total wafer revenue. Source: https://investor.tsmc.com/english/encrypt/files/encrypt_file/qr/phase4_reports/2026-04/bd8eb0403902fdea59a2f5e390e48d010b50edc9/1Q26%20EarningsRelease_WoG.pdf

[Fact] TSMC 2025 annual report states that 2nm technology entered high-volume manufacturing in Q4 2025 with good yield and expects a fast ramp in 2026. Source: https://investor.tsmc.com/static/annualReports/2025/english/index.html

[Fact] TSMC 2025 annual report describes ongoing development of advanced packaging and 3D chip stacking technologies including CoWoS, InFO, TSMC-SoIC and TSMC-COUPE to support customer needs. Source: https://investor.tsmc.com/static/annualReports/2025/english/index.html

[Inference] The combination of high advanced-node revenue share, high HPC revenue share, 2nm ramp commentary and advanced-packaging technology development supports the thesis that TSMC is an upstream bottleneck for AI compute supply.
[Hypothesis] If AI accelerator demand remains constrained by package-integrated compute modules, TSMC’s CoWoS/SoIC expansion pace may be as important as wafer starts for customer allocation.

[Speculation] The market may under-separate the different constraints inside the TSMC bottleneck: leading-edge wafer capacity, advanced packaging, HBM availability, substrate supply and customer capex timing may each bind at different times.
falsification_plan: Downgrade the thesis if TSMC quarterly reports show HPC revenue share or sequential HPC growth weakening while AI capex claims remain strong.
Downgrade the thesis if advanced-node revenue share falls materially or if 3nm/2nm utilization weakens versus management ramp expectations.
Downgrade the thesis if CoWoS/SoIC commentary indicates supply-demand balance or excess capacity earlier than expected.
Downgrade the thesis if gross margin deteriorates materially because of overseas fab cost, pricing pressure, underutilization or depreciation.
Downgrade the thesis if customer product cycles shift away from TSMC-heavy advanced packaging or if major AI customers reduce allocation commitments.
Downgrade the thesis if HBM, substrates, networking, power or data-center deployment become the dominant bottleneck and TSMC capacity is no longer the binding constraint.
Downgrade the thesis if geopolitical disruption, export controls or customer dual-sourcing materially reduce shipment visibility.
next_research_tasks: Verify the latest TSMC quarterly deck and transcript for exact management language on CoWoS, SoIC, 2nm, capex and AI demand durability.

Separate the bottleneck into wafer capacity, CoWoS, SoIC, HBM, ABF substrates, interposers, advanced test and final system deployment; score each node by supplier count, lead time, capex intensity and customer qualification difficulty.
Track quarterly advanced-node mix: 3nm, 5nm, 7nm and 2nm ramp indicators, including yield and utilization commentary.
Track quarterly HPC revenue share and sequential growth to test whether AI demand is still flowing through TSMC rather than only through downstream headlines.
Compare TSMC advanced-packaging expansion with OSAT spillover beneficiaries and substrate/HBM suppliers to determine where the current binding constraint has migrated.
Map customer exposure across NVIDIA, AMD, Broadcom/custom ASIC customers, Apple, hyperscaler internal ASIC programs and other HPC customers.
Review capex approvals and fab construction updates for Taiwan, Arizona, Japan and Germany to assess cost, timing and margin impact.
Build a falsification dashboard with triggers for HPC mix, advanced-node mix, gross margin, capex guidance, CoWoS/SoIC capacity language, 2nm milestones and geopolitical/export-control changes.
risks: Advanced packaging scarcity may ease faster than expected if TSMC, OSAT partners and substrate suppliers expand capacity ahead of AI accelerator demand.
2nm ramp execution risk: yield, cost, customer adoption or schedule could disappoint relative to the current fast-ramp expectation.
AI demand risk: hyperscaler capex or accelerator orders could slow if model economics, power availability, regulation or deployment returns weaken.
Margin risk: overseas fab expansion, depreciation, utility cost, labor cost and geopolitical diversification may pressure gross margin.
Customer concentration and allocation risk: AI accelerator demand is tied to a limited set of large customers and product cycles.
Technology substitution risk: chip architectures, in-house accelerators, alternative foundries, packaging architectures or photonics integration could change the bottleneck map.
Geopolitical and export-control risk: Taiwan Strait tensions, U.S.-China restrictions, or supply-chain localization policies could impair confidence, shipments or customer allocation.
HBM and substrate dependency risk: even if TSMC expands wafers and packaging, HBM supply, ABF substrates, power delivery or system-level bottlenecks may limit final accelerator output.
deep_reports.supply_chain_position: Theme: Technology / AI infrastructure. Demand drivers: hyperscale AI capex, training/inference accelerators, custom ASICs, chiplet architectures, HBM integration, lower-power high-bandwidth compute. Supply-chain map: cloud AI demand -> accelerator designers such as NVIDIA, AMD, Broadcom/custom ASIC customers and internal hyperscaler silicon teams -> leading-edge foundry wafers at 5nm/3nm/2nm -> advanced packaging and 3D integration including CoWoS, SoIC, InFO and related interconnect technologies -> HBM suppliers and substrate/OSAT partners -> AI servers, racks and data centers. TSMC sits at the scarce manufacturing node where leading-edge logic fabrication and high-density package integration meet.
deep_reports.thesis_cn: 台积电的核心卡点不只是晶圆代工规模，而是同时掌握 AI 加速器所需的领先制程晶圆产能、先进封装能力和客户验证生态。AI GPU、ASIC、chiplet 与 HBM 集成需要 3nm/5nm、未来 2nm，以及 CoWoS、SoIC 等封装/3D 集成能力。2026 Q1 可核验事实显示，台积电美元收入为 359 亿美元，同比增长 40.6%；7nm 及以下先进制程占晶圆收入 74%；HPC 平台占收入 61%。这些数据支持其作为 AI 基建上游关键产能瓶颈的研究优先级。后续必须继续拆分真正的约束来源：晶圆、CoWoS/SoIC、HBM 供应、ABF/基板、或客户自身部署节奏。
deep_reports.thesis_en: [Inference] TSMC’s chokepoint is not merely foundry scale, but its combined control of leading-edge wafer capacity, advanced packaging, and customer-validated manufacturing ecosystems required for AI accelerators. AI GPUs, custom ASICs, chiplets, and HBM-integrated systems depend on 3nm/5nm, future 2nm, and CoWoS/SoIC-class packaging and 3D integration. Verifiable Q1 2026 facts show US$35.9B revenue, up 40.6% year over year; 7nm-and-below technologies represented 74% of wafer revenue; and HPC represented 61% of revenue. These support TSMC’s priority as an upstream capacity bottleneck for AI infrastructure. The next research question is whether the binding constraint is wafers, CoWoS/SoIC, HBM supply, substrates, or customer deployment timing.
